title: AI Makes You Better at the Task, But Your Brain Learns Nothing
angle: A randomized trial with 487 consultants: people using generative AI scored much higher on data-science tasks they had never done before (up to +49 percentage points). When the tool was taken away, there was no evidence they had learned anything. It surprises because most people assume that doing the work with AI also teaches them how to do it. Researchers call this 'temporary upskilling'. Close on the practical tip: try it yourself first, then check your work with AI. Footage: students at laptops, offices, someone staring at a blank page.

title: Why Nobody Noticed Your Mistake
angle: The video reveals that others notice our flaws 50% less than we think due to the Spotlight Effect. It uses generic city footage of crowds to show how everyone is focused on themselves, not you.

title: Why You Forget Everything When You Walk Into a Room
angle: Shows people walking through doors, then blanking. Explains the doorway effect: the brain treats a new room as a new event and files the old thought away. Ends with a tip: go back to the original spot, or say the goal out loud.

title: Why You Like People Near You More
angle: The video explains the Propinquity Effect, where physical distance is the biggest predictor of friendship, surprising viewers by showing their 'choices' are just geography.

title: You Like It Because You Chose It Before
angle: A Dresden study finds that repeated choices alone raise how much we prefer and rate an option. Shows the same lunch spot, playlist and route, then asks how much of your taste is just repetition.

title: Habits Form Faster Than You Think
angle: Calm narration over everyday routines (morning coffee, phone check, commute): the '66 days' myth versus newer research showing automaticity can form quickly, so tiny repeated actions matter more than waiting for a magic number. Counter-intuitive and gives a practical takeaway.

title: Why Beginners Feel Like Experts
angle: This video explains the Dunning-Kruger effect through the 'Peak of Mount Ignorant,' showing why people with the least knowledge often have the most confidence while experts doubt themselves.

title: Why Your Brain Can't Let Go of Unfinished Tasks
angle: The video explains the Zeigarnik Effect, where your brain creates a state of mental tension that only resolves when a task is completed, which is why your to-do list feels physically heavy.

title: Decision Fatigue: Why You Buy Junk at Night
angle: The video reveals how the brain's willpower is a finite resource, explaining why we make poor decisions like impulse buying or snacking late in the day when our 'mental energy' is depleted.

title: Why You Feel a Phantom Phone Vibration
angle: This video explains the sensory hallucination of phantom pocket vibrations through tactile habituation and neural misfires. It surprises viewers by revealing that their nervous system is simply over-predicting sensations due to constant device checking.

title: Why You Always Pick the Middle Option
angle: This video exposes the Decoy Effect, showing how companies deliberately introduce a useless third option to trick your brain into buying the most expensive item. It surprises viewers by revealing that their purchasing choices are heavily manipulated by simple spatial framing.

title: Why Favors Make Friends
angle: It reveals the counter-intuitive truth that asking someone for a small favor actually makes them like you more, rather than doing a favor for them.

title: Why Everyone Is Not Staring At You
angle: This video exposes the Spotlight Effect, revealing how your brain hallucinates that strangers are judging your every micro-movement. It surprises viewers by proving that people barely remember what you wore an hour ago.

title: The Pratfall Effect: Why Mistakes Make You Likable
angle: A person acts perfectly versus a person who spills their coffee. The video explains that small blunders make highly competent people seem more human and approachable to others.

title: Why You See It Everywhere Now
angle: The video explains the Baader-Meinhof phenomenon where your brain, after learning a new word or seeing a specific car, starts 'filtering' it into your conscious awareness, making it look like a global coincidence.

title: Why You Get Great Ideas in the Shower
angle: Explains the 'shower effect' where mind-wandering during routine, non-demanding tasks releases dopamine and shifts the brain into the default mode network, unlocking creative epiphanies. Shows fast-paced b-roll of flowing water, city walks, and sudden realizations.

title: Why Switching Apps Makes You Tired
angle: Explains the psychological cost of micro-task switching (attention residue). Moving between casual apps like messages, feeds, and browser tabs drains cognitive glucose even when you feel like you are just relaxing.

title: Why You Hate Your Recorded Voice
angle: Explains why hearing a recording of yourself makes you cringe due to bone conduction vibrating your skull, making your internal voice sound deeper and richer than it actually is. It surprises viewers by revealing everyone else hears the 'cringe' version and thinks it is completely normal.

title: Why Rereading Makes You Forget
angle: It reveals that highlighting and rereading text creates a false sense of familiarity called 'the illusion of competence' rather than actual memory.

title: Why You Refuse to Sleep When Exhausted
angle: Explains Bedtime Revenge Procrastination, where people stay up late scrolling because it is the only part of the day they feel in total control over. It turns bedtime guilt into an eye-opening psychological revelation.

title: Why You Can't Eat Without Watching Something
angle: Explains sensory pairing and cue-conditioned dopamine loops: your brain has linked the act of chewing with passive video consumption, making quiet eating feel agonizingly under-stimulating. It reveals how decoupling them resets your satiety signals.

title: Why You Freeze Before Starting Work
angle: Explains the psychological phenomenon of task paralysis and the amygdala hijacking your prefrontal cortex when an ambition feels ambiguous, revealing the counter-intuitive 2-minute fix that tricks the brain into action.

title: 5 Biological Speed-Limiters Keeping You From Being Superhuman
angle: Your muscles are strong enough to lift a car and snap your own bones, but your brain keeps a 'governor' on your strength at 30% to prevent self-destruction—until a life-or-death emergency overrides it.

title: The 10-Second Balance Glitch
angle: An interactive test that forces the viewer to stand up and try a physical impossibility. It highlights the science of center of gravity and neuromuscular feedback. It triggers comments from people trying to 'beat' the glitch and failing.

title: The Ghost Color Glitch
angle: An interactive optical illusion where viewers stare at a specific dot to see a 'ghost' color on a gray screen. This forces 100% focus and prompts comments when the effect works.

title: The Hidden Setting Draining Your Battery and Privacy
angle: The video reveals a specific deep-layer smartphone setting—Significant Locations or System Services—that maps every movement. It challenges the viewer to check it right now to see their own 'secret map,' triggering comments from shocked users.

title: The Ghost Hand Floating Glitch
angle: A live interactive test where the viewer stands in a doorway and pushes their arms outward against the frame for 30 seconds. The physical reflex causes their arms to float upward involuntarily afterward. This forces 100% retention as they must stay for the duration and comment their results.

title: Why Stores Doubled Shopping Cart Sizes
angle: Reveals how doubling the physical volume of shopping carts tricks the human brain into buying 40% more items without realizing it, exposing grocery retail architecture. Comment trigger asks viewers whether they grab a basket or cart and what their biggest accidental grocery bill was.
